title: Subagent Telemetry, Observability, and Interactive Chat Tracking

context.problem: Subagent invocations in the companion app currently suffer from broken telemetry: subagent names, roles, and prompts are lost due to a mismatch between Antigravity parameters and an assumed array wrapper; active counts remain zero; and the inner activities of subagents (web searches, file reads, terminal commands, outputs) are completely hidden from the chat conversation and the subagents team room both during live streaming and when resuming past conversations.
constraints: Android Termux resource limits: server memory must remain under 80 MB, 2 CPU threads max
Screen reader first: TalkBack and Jieshuo (CSR) must announce subagent identity, actions, and completion clearly without emoji noise or wide tables
Zero disk transcript corruption: CLI transcripts in ~/.gemini/antigravity-cli/brain/ are strictly read-only append-only
Tool output bounds: previews strictly bounded to 16 KB to prevent EventLog buffer overflows, SSE disconnects, and WebView freezes on mobile
Backward compatibility: 100% pass on existing test suites (run_ui_tests.cjs, run_backend_tests.py, run_tests.py)

functional.text: Accurate Subagent Identification & Identity Extraction: Top-level Role, TypeName, and Prompt parameters parsed directly from invoke_subagent, eliminating 'وكيل جديد' fallback and restoring live agent badges and counts.
Deep Subagent Execution Observability: Capture and stream inner child tool calls (search_web, view_file, run_command, send_message) and their outputs directly from child transcripts.
In-Chat Subagent Thread & Cards: Embed live and historical subagent progress directly inside the conversation turn feed with collapsible accordions matching main tool result cards.
Accessible Screen-Reader Telemetry: Announce subagent launches, tool activities, and completions via ARIA live regions and semantic badges without visual-only dependencies.
Full Historical Recovery: When resuming past conversations, auto-discover all child subagent transcripts and restore the complete multi-agent activity stream.

deepDives.title: Dual-Cursor Hierarchical Transcript Poller
deepDives.pressure: Subagent activity occurs in independent child directories while parent run is active; polling multiple directories must not peg mobile CPU or cause file lock errors.
deepDives.decision: Maintain a dictionary of active child cursors in Sessions poller. When an invoke_subagent tool result yields a conversationId, register the child path and poll up to 4 child transcripts per tick with cursor line offsets.
deepDives.failureMode: Child transcript not created yet or slow disk flush; caught with existence checks and retry on next tick without crashing.

deepDives.title: In-Place Chat Thread Rendering & Screen Reader Live Announcements
deepDives.pressure: Visually impaired users using TalkBack or CSR need immediate, clear auditory feedback when subagents start, execute tools, and finish, without overwhelming chatter or visual-only accordions.
deepDives.decision: Render a specialized SubagentThreadCard in the chat feed and announce semantic summary lines (e.g. 'الوكيل: مراجع الكود بدأ فحص الملفات') via aria-live='polite'. Nested tools use the standard accessible details/summary pattern with ARIA expanded states.
deepDives.failureMode: Repeated ARIA announcements stuttering speech; debounced to only announce significant state transitions and new tool names.

deepDives.title: Memory Bounding & Android WebView Protection
deepDives.pressure: Subagents running large code searches or compilation commands can generate hundreds of kilobytes of output, crashing low-memory Android WebViews if unconstrained.
deepDives.decision: Enforce a strict 16 KB preview cap on child tool outputs at both the poller emitter and frontend card renderer, with a clean button to view full content or copy text.
deepDives.failureMode: User needs complete log; remedy is inline copy button reading full text from local file API or disk path.

pros: Complete end-to-end visibility of subagent actions in chat and subagents dialog
Zero new server infrastructure or heavy external dependencies
Preserves full history when resuming past multi-agent conversations
Strict 16 KB bounds ensure mobile battery and memory safety
cons: Polling multiple files introduces small CPU overhead (tested < 5ms per tick)

notes: Additive change in server and web UI; completely backward compatible with existing conversations.

architectures.name: Client-Side Polling via Dedicated Subagent REST Endpoints
architectures.thesis: Separate subagent state into discrete REST endpoints (/api/ai/subagents/{cid}) and require the frontend to poll them independently from the parent SSE stream.

components.name: Subagent REST API
components.note: Reads child transcript on client request

pros: Decouples subagent polling from parent SSE run
cons: Redundant HTTP round-trips causing high battery drain on Android
Out-of-order race conditions between parent chat output and subagent cards
High client timer complexity and connection fatigue

notes: Requires new endpoints and complex client polling logic.

reasoning: Architecture A unifies parent and child telemetry into a single coordinated SSE stream, eliminating mobile battery drain from redundant client HTTP polling.
It leverages the existing 500 ms poller in server/sessions.py with simple cursor line indexing, keeping memory addition under 12 KB.
It provides immediate in-chat visibility and seamless TalkBack/CSR screen-reader accessibility for Ahmed without altering disk transcripts.

findings.subject: repo
findings.title: Subagent invocation parameters look for params.Subagents array instead of direct Role/TypeName

evidence.text: main-ui.js line 877 and line 1673 check data.params.Subagents which is undefined in Antigravity

findings.whyItMatters: Subagents appear as anonymous 'وكيل جديد' or fail to register entirely in the subagent team room and counters.

remedy.text: Directly extract Role, TypeName, and Prompt from params top-level with fallback to legacy array.

findings.subject: repo
findings.title: Sessions poller only reads parent transcript, leaving child subagent transcripts unobserved
findings.whyItMatters: Users cannot observe what subagents are doing (reading files, executing commands, searching web) during turn execution.

remedy.text: Register child conversationId upon subagent creation and drain child transcripts concurrently using line cursors.

lenses.objection: Confirmed by absence of child transcript drain loop

risks.text: Multiple concurrent subagents writing simultaneously could lead to transient read-after-write delays
risks.horizon: under heavy 4+ subagent workloads; mitigated by cursor retries on subsequent 500ms poller ticks
